log.msg: THE VIEWER BUG WORTH REMEMBERING: framework.css's base layer sets iframe { max-width: 100% }, so a frame told to be 3440px wide was laid out at its container's 1766px and THEN scaled by 1766/3440 - the viewer rendered the site at 1766 with '3440 px' written beside it and nothing threw. Found by reading the painted box back (907px where 1766 was expected), not by looking. Fixed with max-width: none on .site-viewer-frame; re-measured 3440 -> scale(0.5134), painted 1766x462, fits.

The corpus cites the standard through the standard's own alias table. /layouts/ landed beside this and had renamed the seed word N-cards to n-wall, with 3-cards an alias of 3-equal and bento an alias of 4-1. Site.js reads /layouts/layouts.json once and resolves aliases, so a record writes whichever word reads best and the chip still lands on the entry. Verified live: all five layout links the three records draw resolve to real entries.

Presentation fix after looking at the 400 shot: the front's tag filter showed all 26 tags, which stood 400px tall on a phone and pushed every site card below the fold on the page whose only job is to show them. It now shows only tags two or more sites carry (6 chips) plus 'every tag' - the wall is above the fold at 400.

Verified headless at 400 and 1920 on :8123 - index, a blocked-embed record, a framed record, a tag page, the tag index, the docs front and a doc note: no console errors, no thrown errors, no md-errors, no missing Material Icons ligatures, no document overflow at either width. Clicked through from the HOMEPAGE card to a site to a tag with no typed urls. Corpus is 3 sites, 26 tags, 3.4MB for 15 jpegs.

assign.outcome:
**`/websites/` is live — the corpus, its class, its json and its tools, with three real sites in it.** One record per site (`site/<name>.json`), five jpegs beside it, and pages that render nothing but the record.

![a record page: four widths side by side](/framework/ai/2026-09-08/websites-db/shots/embed-1920.jpg)

**Open first:** [the corpus](/websites/) (the wall + a tag filter) · [wikipedia-css](/websites/wikipedia-css/) (the **live resizable viewer** — drag the slider, the real site relays itself at 3440 and is scaled to fit) · [tag/3-holy-grail](/websites/tag/3-holy-grail/) (walk sideways).

**The record** is two halves that never touch: a machine writes `url title captured_at embed shots scan`, a person writes `layout sections tags responsive notes` after LOOKING at the shots. `write_record()` merges by whole top-level key, so re-shooting a site next year keeps its tags. [`doc/schema.md`](/websites/doc/schema/).

**The tools** ([`doc/tools.md`](/websites/doc/tools/)) — `shoot.mjs` (five jpegs at 400/1280/1920/3440 + a 1280x4000 long shot; `embed` read from `x-frame-options` and CSP `frame-ancestors`, not by trying), `scan.mjs` (every landmark at all four widths with its computed `display`, grid tracks, `position` — plus **`side_by_side`**, the count of children whose tops line up, which is the column count a person would count whatever CSS made it; CSS off the wire, because `cssRules` throws on 5 of 5 cross-origin sheets), `index.mjs` (the manifest the pages read — production is static, nothing crawls).

**The seeds, measured:** MDN and Wikipedia are both `3-holy-grail` at 1280/1920/3440 and `1-flow` at 400, capped at 1416 and 1596px; Stripe is `1-centered` at 1920/3440 and `1-flow` at 1280 — full-bleed bands with a 1232px measure inside. Wikipedia reaches three columns **two ways at once** (main is a grid of article + rail; the contents list is a separate positioned column) — the argument for keeping the CSS technique as a separate tag.

**Three defects found and fixed, each measured not guessed:** framework.css's base `iframe { max-width: 100% }` silently rendered a "3440" frame at 1766px with the right label on it (painted box read 907 where 1766 was expected); `scan.mjs`'s first `[role]` sweep spent Stripe's whole landmark budget on ten identical `<svg role="img">` logos; the front's 26-chip filter row stood 400px tall on a phone and pushed every site below the fold. [`doc/decisions.md`](/websites/doc/decisions/).

**Verified** headless at 400 and 1920 across the index, both embed cases, a tag page, the tag index and both doc pages: no console errors, no `.md-error`, no missing icon ligatures, no document overflow — and clicked through from the **homepage card** to a site to a tag with no typed urls. All five `/layouts/` links resolve, through the encyclopedia's own alias table (`3-cards` → `/layouts/3-equal/`).

**Left, with reasons:** `site-` is not in `framework/styles/css-scopes.txt` — that file is outside this task's fence; the census is clean and the exact line to add is in `doc/decisions.md`. Section layouts are not yet indexed as a set (`sections[].layout` is all there; it wants one more index in `index.mjs`, not a new idea). Three sites is a seed, not a corpus — the tools take the next thirty.
